candidates.statement: For the purpose of this article we shall concentrate on the combinatorial aspect of this theory connected with non--crossing partitions [@Kreweras] and mentioned above free cumulants, which were introduced by Speicher [@Speicher1994; @Speicher1997; @Speicher1998].

There are many equivalent definitions of the transition measure of a Young diagram [@VershikKerov1995asymptoticbehavior; @Kerov1993transition; @Kerov1999differential; @OkounkovVershik1996; @Biane1998; @Okounkov2000randompermutations] and for the sake of completeness we shall recall them in the following.
Nevertheless, we shall use in this article only the description from Section [\[subsec:transition1\]](#subsec:transition1){reference-type="ref" reference="subsec:transition1"}.
Similarly we shall interpret pairs of Abelian algebras ${\mathfrak{B}}\subset{\mathfrak{A}}$ equipped with a map ${\mathbb{E}}:{\mathfrak{A}}\rightarrow{\mathfrak{B}}$.

The conditional expectation ${\mathbb{E}}_{{\mathbb{C}}({{S}}_{A})} :{\mathbb{C}}({{S}}_{A\cup\{\ast\}})\rightarrow {\mathbb{C}}({{S}}_{A})$ will be given by the orthogonal projection, i.e. $${\mathbb{E}}_{{\mathbb{C}}({{S}}_{A})}(\sigma)=\begin{cases} \sigma & \text{if } \sigma\in{{S}}_{A} \\ 0 & \text{if } \sigma\notin{{S}}_{A} \end{cases}= \begin{cases} \sigma & \text{if } \sigma(\ast)=\ast, \\ 0 & \text{if } \sigma(\ast)\neq \ast.\end{cases}$$ In the rest of this article, when it does not lead to confusions, instead of ${\mathbb{E}}_{{\mathbb{C}}({{S}}_{A})}$ we shall simply write ${\mathbb{E}}$.

We define moments of the Jucys--Murphy element by $$M^{\mathop{\mathrm{JM}}}_k={\mathbb{E}}(J^k)= \sum_{a_1,\dots,a_k\in A } {\mathbb{E}}[ (a_1 \ast) \cdots (a_k \ast) ] \in {\mathbb{C}}({{S}}_{A}). \label{eq:wielkasuma}$$ In Section [\[subsec:momentmap\]](#subsec:momentmap){reference-type="ref" reference="subsec:momentmap"} of we shall consider an extension of this concept.

We consider a filtration on the commutative algebra generated by $\Sigma_{k_1,\dots,k_m}\in{\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})$ by setting $$\label{eq:filtration} \deg \Sigma_{k_1,\dots,k_m}=(k_1+1)+(k_2+1)+\cdots+(k_m+1).$$ It is easy to check that the elements from the family $\Sigma_{k_1,\dots,k_m}\in{\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})$ indexed by integer $m\geq 0$ and $k_1\geq \cdots \geq k_m\geq 1$ are linearly independent and therefore this definition makes sense but it is not clear that this formula indeed defines a filtration; we shall prove it in Corollary [\[cor:filtration\]](#cor:filtration){reference-type="ref" reference="cor:filtration"}.

The reason for studying this filtration is that---as we shall see in Theorem [\[theo:kontrolastopnia\]](#theo:kontrolastopnia){reference-type="ref" reference="theo:kontrolastopnia"}---elements $M^{\mathop{\mathrm{JM}}}_k\in{\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})$ and $\Sigma_{k_1,\dots,k_m}\in{\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})$ generate the same commutative algebra denoted by $\mathfrak{P}$ and filtration [\[eq:filtration\]](#eq:filtration){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:filtration"} is induced by the gradation [\[eq:gradation\]](#eq:gradation){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:gradation"}.
However, it should be understood that by a change of labels these constructions can be performed for any finite ordered set $X$.

We define $\pi_{\mathop{\mathrm{fat}}}$, called fat partition of $\pi$, to be a pair partition of the $2n$--element ordered set $\{1,1',2,2',\dots,n,n'\}$ given by $$\pi_{\mathop{\mathrm{fat}}}= \big\{ \{ \pi_{s,t}',\pi_{s,t+1} \} : 1\leq s \leq r \text{ and } 1 \leq t \leq l_s \big\},$$ where it should be understood that $\pi_{s,l_s+1}=\pi_{s,1}$.

Due to the canonical bijection between $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ and $\{1',2',\dots,n'\}$ we can identify $\mathop{\mathrm{NC}}(1,2,\dots,n)$ with $\mathop{\mathrm{NC}}(1',2',\dots,n')$ and in the future we shall sometimes regard $\pi_{\mathop{\mathrm{comp}}}$ as an element of $\mathop{\mathrm{NC}}(1,2,\dots,n)$ and sometimes as an element of $\mathop{\mathrm{NC}}(1',2',\dots,n')$.

We shall also consider the inverse of the Kreweras complementation map: for $\pi, \rho\in\mathop{\mathrm{NC}}(1,2,\dots,n)$ we have $\pi_{{\mathop{\mathrm{comp}}^{-1}}}=\rho$ if and only if $\pi=\rho_{\mathop{\mathrm{comp}}}$.

In Section [\[sec:proofs\]](#sec:proofs){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:proofs"} we shall define the most important tool of this article: a certain map $\Phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{P}}}_{{\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})}$ from the set of partitions to ${\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})$.

Then $$\Sigma_\pi:=\Phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{P}}}_{{\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})}(\pi)=\Sigma_{k_1,\dots,k_t},$$ where $\Sigma_{k_1,\dots,k_t}\in{\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})$ on the right--hand side should be understood as in Section [\[subsec:definicjasigma\]](#subsec:definicjasigma){reference-type="ref" reference="subsec:definicjasigma"}. :::
To the arcs on the boundary of the circle between points $1,1',2,2',\dots,n,n'$ and to the lines of $\pi_{\mathop{\mathrm{fat}}}$ we shall glue two collections of discs.
The boundary of each hole corresponds to one of the cycles of $\pi_{\mathop{\mathrm{fat}}}\circ c$ and we shall glue this hole with a disc from the second collection.

We shall glue to the hole $\rho_s$ only the first collection of discs that we considered in Section [\[subsec:zaklejanie\]](#subsec:zaklejanie){reference-type="ref" reference="subsec:zaklejanie"}, i.e. the discs which correspond to the blocks of the partition $\pi^s$.

Then $$\Sigma\Big( \prod_{s} \pi^s \Big)=\prod_{1\leq s\leq r} \Sigma_{\pi^s},$$ where the multiplication on the left hand side should be understood as the $\rho$--ordered product of partitions and on the right hand side it should be understood as the usual product of commuting elements in ${\mathbb{C}}(\widetilde{{{S}}_{\infty}})$. :::

It follows that there is an element of $\rho_2\setminus\pi^2_1$, namely $c$, which is connected by $\sigma$ with $a\in\pi_1^1$, and the latter element must be connected by $\sigma$ with the elements of $\pi^2_1$.
From the very definition of multiplication one can see that every partition $\sigma$ which appears in $M^{\mathop{\mathrm{P}}}_\rho$ must fulfill $\sigma\geq \rho_{{\mathop{\mathrm{comp}}^{-1}}}$.
